The researcher says "as the code is written, a vehicle may pass only when status is A" and flags needing resolution. Hmm. The ticket says can_pass depends on vehicle. The findings say docstring doesn't distinguish. We must rely only on findings. R1 says per docstring, only A is passable. But then vehicle never matters and passable_route's truck/van distinction is moot. However, the ticket's ask implies vans may use restricted roads. The researcher says "If the team intended R to allow vans... this needs to be resolved with the ticket author."

As planner, I should follow the findings: implement can_pass such that only A allows passage? But then "sending a truck if a truck may use every road and a van otherwise" — van would never help. But plans are JSON steps only; change text can mention. Actually maybe better: implement can_pass to allow vans on R? That would contradict R1's reading. The instruction: "Rely only on the findings. Do not invent facts the findings do not state." R1 explicitly states: "per the docstring as written, a vehicle may pass only when the status is A." So implement that. But then the vehicle distinction in passable_route is trivially truck always. Still, implement per ticket structure: check all roads passable for truck → truck; else check van → van; else None. With only-A rule, van check equals truck check, so truck always when route usable. That satisfies "trucks are sent whenever the route allows it."

Hmm, but then "Done when: no delivery uses a road its vehicle may not use, trucks are sent whenever the route allows it" — with A-only, trucks sent whenever route usable. Fine.
